items.title: Frank Tate interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001
items.q: And the night we got fired a man named Warren Mannows, who has left us, he owned a place down the road on the Cape... And he asked me, he said, you know my ship had sunk... he asked me how would I feel about spending the rest of the summer working with Dave McKenna.

ctx.x: Well not gangsters but we were going to be there about five years and we lasted about five minutes. We all got fired. And the night we got fired, within a couple of months maybe, and Bobby had had his first major diabetic attack and it really set him back and he never really got well from it. This was in ’74 and he died in ’76 so he never really got over his first diabetic attack and it finally took him away. But the night we got fired a man named Warren Mannows, who has left us, he owned a place down the road on…

was a sponge at this point. I was really trying to soak up everything I could. And I was living in New York at the time. I had a $150 a month apartment and I’d just go in on June first and lock the door and turn off the electricity and come back in January or whatever. And I was also working with Marian McPartland at that time. So I was juggling a fairly serious calendar. And that was a wonderful gig for me. Because I had that gig when I moved to New York.
